name: Counting subsets
whenToUse: Count all subsets, subsets with at least a few elements, or subsets of a given parity of size.
example: Subsets of $\{1, 2, \ldots, 10\}$ with at least two elements: $2^{10} - \binom{10}{0} - \binom{10}{1} = 1024 - 1 - 10 = 1013$.
pitfall: $2^n$ includes the empty set and the full set. Subtract whichever the problem excludes; nonempty subsets number $2^n - 1$.
derivation: Each element is either in or out, giving $2^n$ choices. Expanding $(1 - 1)^n = 0$ with the binomial theorem shows the even and odd sizes balance.
